_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Progress gets its own top-bar icon and a rebuilt overview
detail: Progress opens directly from the landing page top bar instead of the language settings chip.
A coverage ring, Known / Practice / New breakdown and expandable answer history replace the old statistics grid.
The dialog opens immediately, handles empty data and failures, supports retry and keyboard closing, and ignores stale requests after closing or changing source.
Removed the misleading complete-sentence percentage calculated from a partially loaded example corpus.
Coverage and counts share one deduplicated snapshot from the current vocabulary and recorded knowledge.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: dual song selector with offline probe songs and live online TURBO intake (Spotify URL, track ID, search query, or manual paste)
detail: Added segmented picker tabs: choose between curated offline playlist (30 songs) or generate custom songs online with TURBO.
Online intake supports Spotify track URLs, Spotify track IDs (22 chars), song title & artist searches via LRCLIB, and direct manual lyrics paste.
Integrated client TURBO engine execution on the fly with live status progress, caching newly generated songs for seamless switching.
Added topbar shortcut pill '⚡ Online TURBO' and auto-detection of Spotify URLs in search inputs.

entries.summary: Study sets: larger rank numbers, brighter legend and darker skipped progress
detail: Removed the hash from each frequency range and enlarged the numbers with heavier weight and vertical padding.
Legend counts use the main text colour for clearer contrast.
Skipped cards use a darker slate-grey fill in set progress bars and the matching legend swatch.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: Spotify-style minimalist layout with target lyrics, English subtitles underneath, mobile bottom-sheet, and Fluency design integration
detail: Replaced dense audit layout with Spotify-style minimalist lyrics flow: prominent target text in Space Grotesk with clean English gloss directly underneath.
Unified design system with Fluency's industrial dark palette (--bg-primary, --bg-card, --border-color, --font-emphasis).
Added mobile-first responsive bottom-sheet modal with drag handle and safe-area padding for one-handed inspection on phones.
Added topbar subtitle toggle pill ('EN line') to switch English line translation visibility.

entries.summary: Level Estimator audit: starting level placement fix, SENSE_CYCLE POS resolution, keyboard controls, and CEFR indicators
detail: Fixed off-by-one level placement where learners were routed to a 100% completed level; now routes to first unseen card.
Resolved SENSE_CYCLE part-of-speech handling so grouped nouns and verbs are sampled and labelled properly.
Increased shard candidate attempts to 48 to prevent premature aborts on columnar releases.
Added full keyboard shortcuts (Space/Enter to flip, 1/2 or Arrow keys to answer, Escape to close) and modal backdrop dismissal.
Added visual progress track and CEFR stage mapping on results screen.

entries.summary: Song lyrics view: interactive lyric reader with token quick-view, sense assignments, entities, and ad-libs
detail: Added lyrics-view mode accessible from learning settings and the artist setup card in lyrics mode.
Browse the 30-song offline playlist with searchable picker and song-by-song navigation.
Interactive lyric lines with automatic classification and inline badges for entities, idioms/MWEs, interjections/ad-libs, and vocabulary.
Quick-view modal inspecting surface elisions, primary sense assignments, entity cultural descriptions, and alternate Spanish senses with keyboard navigation.

entries.summary: Landing page: centred section labels and wider set cards in a 2 × 2 grid
detail: Choose level, Choose a set and Practice errors have equal spacing above and below their labels.
Set cards are about 20% shorter and arranged in two columns, with frequency rank ranges visible on phones and desktop.
The selected set retains its accent ring without enlarging or shifting the card.

entries.summary: Cards are no longer named after a phrase they appear in: é cites ser, not "não é"
detail: A card's dictionary form skips headwords with more words than the card's own word (não é on é, por qué on por, cinto de segurança on cinto), unless it is the same spelling written apart (porfavor).
Look up links on é now open WordReference and Reverso for ser; they searched "não é".
With Merge Lemmas on, the back of é reads ser, not "não é · ser"; não, por and do read não, por and de.
Same rule as the release's lemma column (11276edc), already live on es and pt v23.

entries.summary: UNISON post-audit release: metadata contract, clean possessives, split card partitioning, and MWE production cues
detail: Split cards: prevent Card 2 from repeating the whole Card 1 menu when it has no distinct primary senses; retain expression senses on base cards.
Card metadata pills: suppress grammatical jargon tags (transitive, intransitive, copular) while keeping companion prepositions, register, and regional badges intact.
English to target production: display [phrase] scope badge on multi-word expression prompts so learners know a phrase is expected.
Portuguese & Spanish decks: updated with Decision 0030 sense/metadata contract, cleaner possessives (seu -> your/his/her), and companion disambiguation (falar + com / + de).

entries.summary: Vocabulary choice: switching and progress carry-over stated; hover text says words start most common first
detail: Intro under 'Choose your flashcard vocabulary source' now ends: You can switch at any time, and the words you learn carry over between the two modes.
Desktop hover text on Everyday speech: 'Starts with the most common words in films and TV shows'; on Your music: 'Starts with the most common words in the music you listen to'.
The in-study vocabulary picker shares the intro wording.

entries.summary: One tutorial in three chapters: Studying a card, Smart Skip, Speech or music
detail: Replaces the separate quick tutorial and full card tour. The ? button and Help open it directly; chapter names along the top jump to any chapter.

Studying a card (9 steps): the full card tour with the essentials folded in — recall and flip, how common the word is, kind of word, dictionary form, meanings, choosing a meaning, how common each meaning is, examples and where they come from, swipe to grade.

Cut: Useful extras and Hear it. Merged: the back's repeated 'The word', 'How often it is said' into 'How common the word is', and 'Where the example is from' into the example note. No more tap-to-continue tasks.
Smart Skip and Speech or music are now pages of their own, showing a copy of the real switch and the Vocabulary picker, with examples in the language being taught.
Each chapter ends with Start studying or Next: <chapter> →.

entries.summary: Skipped cards fill each set bar from the right in light grey
detail: Choose a set: with Smart Skip on, the cards it sets aside take a light-grey share of each set pill from the right, so a level starts partly filled.
The Skipped legend swatch is the same grey; known/practice/new shares are now measured against the full slot.

entries.summary: Smart Skip row on the level box shows more example words, in English
detail: The 'Skipping …' / 'Look-alikes like …' line now lists up to eight words (the row trims to fit), as English words (family, minute, important) instead of the Spanish forms.

entries.summary: Set pills show their word ranks on desktop
detail: Choose a set: on screens 760px and wider each pill reads its frequency-rank range (e.g. 26–50) instead of the set number; phones keep the number.

entries.summary: Landing page: English example words, set legend reordered with a Skipped count, tidier Smart Skip pages
detail: Level box: example words are now English meanings, up to eight on desktop (five on phones); 'Level N' and 'Words a–b' share one font size.
Choose a set: legend reads New, Practice, Known at the size of 'Set 1', and adds a hatched Skipped count when Smart Skip is on.
Smart Skip page: the Skipped words menu always opens on Look-alikes (or the first category when look-alikes are off).
Smart Skip page and Advanced options sheet: bordered card rows, quiet count pills, full-width Done button.

entries.summary: Vocabulary choice now says progress carries over and you can switch any time
detail: The line under 'Choose your flashcard vocabulary source' adds: What you learn carries over, and you can switch at any time.
Shown on the inline choose screen (desktop and mobile) and in the in-study vocabulary picker; both read the same wording.

entries.summary: Consistent username wording throughout the profile flow
detail: Profile labels, guidance, validation and playlist sign-in messages now say username.
Existing usernames, saved profiles and learning progress are preserved.

entries.summary: Birthday is optional when choosing a learning profile
detail: Leave day and month blank to look up profiles by name alone.
A supplied birthday narrows matching names; profiles without a birthday remain discoverable.
Partially entered or invalid birthdays still receive inline feedback.

entries.summary: A clearer, quieter welcome and profile screen
detail: Welcome offers a clear saved-progress path and a lighter guest option.
The profile form has one heading, shorter guidance and no repeated welcome pitch.

entries.summary: Quick tutorial first, with the full card tour in Help
detail: The tutorial introduction now starts with the essential lesson, including the correct pronunciation controls.
The full card tour remains an explicit option in Help and the introduction.
All five first-time UX audit recommendations are implemented and recorded.

entries.summary: Clarify learning language prompt, add known-languages primer, and expand tutorial notes
detail: Prompt explicitly asks for 'Choose the language you’re learning' to avoid confusion for non-native English speakers.
Add post-language selection primer asking which languages the learner already knows to filter look-alikes via Smart Skip.
Expand tutorial with Smart Skip explanation and reassure learners that they can switch between Speech and Lyrics anytime with progress saved.

entries.summary: Names and birthdays identify separate learning profiles
detail: Enter a username/name and birthday day/month, with inline validation and no birth year.
Matching profiles show language and last study date; an exact match can always create a separate profile.
Existing initials and all progress keep their original IDs; selected profiles remain remembered on this device.
Saved sets are isolated by profile; the progress backend now includes a shared profile directory.

entries.summary: A shorter first lesson and one-time swipe guidance
detail: Automatic onboarding covers reveal, pronunciation, grading and moving on; Help retains the full card tour.
The first real card reveal shows swipe guidance outside the card until a successful grading swipe.

entries.summary: Reliable keyboard sign-in and phrases-panel resume
detail: Study shortcuts pause while signing in, so Enter submits Continue normally.
Stopping on a phrases panel saves the parent word; older panel snapshots recover by word.

entries.summary: Spanish cognate mapping for Portuguese learners
detail: Spanish is now available as a known language for Portuguese cognate filtering.
Maps each shown meaning through the Spanish dictionary and CogNet; 4,257 of 10,000 current Portuguese cards qualify at the initial 0.80 cutoff.
English mappings are preserved; false friends and cards with unmatched meanings remain in study.

entries.summary: Clearer main-page level and account controls
detail: Level example words exclude phrases and multi-word expressions, with slightly brighter text.
Selected level is larger with less vertical padding.
Language and learner initials are larger; tutorial and settings icons are white.

entries.summary: Tutorial fits its actual available space, including Bigger text
detail: Measured card height from the rendered tutorial area after navigation appears, replacing fixed window-height allowances.
Reserved header and button space, including app text zoom, and held card dimensions steady between steps.
Kept scrolling inside card content and independently inside desktop explanations when needed.

entries.summary: SpanishDict senses sharing a context are one row again; topic chips show only when they tell rows apart
detail: kilo: "kilo" and "kilogram" are one SpanishDict meaning (context "kilogram") and now share one row instead of two rows with separate meters; irse "to go" / "to leave" (to exit a place) likewise. Context grouping had been switched off for every provider on 2026-09-29 because Wiktionary contexts are labels ("intransitive"); it is back for SpanishDict only.
The 10% main-card floor measures a SpanishDict context as a whole, as the card shows it, so a meaning split 2 + 2 between kilo and kilogram is not dropped.

Topic chips (mostly Portuguese Wiktionary) appear only when they tell a row from another row with the same translation, and only the most specific one: massa "dough" lost "cooking | food | lifestyle", garganta's two "throat" rows lost "anatomy | medicine | sciences". The topics stay in each row's (i) note.
Display only: no WSD, release or menu change.

entries.summary: Tutorial layout grows with the browser while card size stays steady
detail: Desktop cards use the available window height and width, with room reserved for navigation.
The tutorial header stays fully visible, and explanations spread across wider screens.
Opening meanings keeps the card size constant; mobile retains its separate height budget and internal scrolling.

entries.summary: Taller desktop tutorial cards and no practice-skip button
detail: Removed Skip this practice; the top-right close button remains available.
Wide desktop cards are about 17% taller while preserving space for Back and Next.
Narrow desktop layouts put the explanation and navigation beside the card, allowing a taller card without pushing buttons off-screen.
Phone cards reserve space for the longest explanation and remain the same height throughout the tutorial.
